Siemens Aktiengesellschaft and Siemens Ltd., China v. Ningbo Qishuai Electric Appliance Co., Ltd., Gong Yinqi, et al. — dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition

【Ruling Summary】

Using the trade name from another enterprise's name that has certain influence and another's registered trademark as one's own trademark and trade name constitutes trademark infringement and unfair competition.

Where the alleged infringer refuses to submit relevant financial evidence, the amount of damages may be determined by reference to the right holder's claims and the evidence provided; where the evidence on record is sufficient to determine that the profits obtained by the infringer from the infringement clearly exceed the maximum statutory damages limit set by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the people's court shall, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the fame of the right holder, the subjective malice of the infringer, the specific circumstances of the infringing acts, and the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder in enforcing its rights, determine the amount of damages exceeding the statutory damages limit.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Case No. 312

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Ningbo Qishuai Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. Domicile: Cidong Industrial Zone, Cixi City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Qiu Pengjun, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Na, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Hechuang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lv Jiamu, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Haitian Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Gong Yinqi, male, born on December 13, 1966, Han Chinese, domiciled in Cixi City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Yong, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Hechuang Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Wang Qiong, female, born on December 28, 1969, Han Chinese, domiciled in Cixi City, Zhejiang Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Yong, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Hechuang Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Siemens Aktiengesellschaft (SIEMENS AKTIENGSELLSCHAFT). Domicile: Werner-von-Siemens-Str. 1, 80333 Munich, Federal Republic of Germany.

Authorized Representative: Dr. Norbert Moritz.

Authorized Representative: Dr. Volkmar Bonn.

Agent ad litem: Sun Jiange, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Kaizheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Ruifeng, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Kaizheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Siemens Ltd., China. Domicile: No. 7, Wangjing Zhonghuan South Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Dr. Song Xiao, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xi, male, employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Jiange, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Kaizheng Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Kunshan Xinweichuang Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 62, Youyi South Road, Zhoushi Town, Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Wu Qianzhi, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Lv Jiamu, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Haitian Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Wu Qianzhi, male, born on October 5, 1986, Han Chinese, domiciled in Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Lv Jiamu, Attorney at Law, Zhejiang Haitian Law Firm.

Appellants Ningbo Qishuai Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qishuai Company), Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong, in the case of dispute over trademark infringement and unfair competition with appellees Siemens Aktiengesellschaft (hereinafter referred to as Siemens Company), Siemens Ltd., China (hereinafter referred to as Siemens China Company) and defendants at first instance Kunshan Xinweichuang Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinweichuang Company) and Wu Qianzhi, appealed against the Civil Judgment (2019) Su Min Chu No. 2 of the Jiangsu High People's Court. This Court docketed the case on July 26, 2022, formed a collegial panel according to law, and held a public hearing. Agents ad litem of Qishuai Company, Li Na and Lv Jiamu; agent ad litem of Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, Zheng Yong; agent ad litem of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, Sun Jiange; and agent ad litem of Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi, Lv Jiamu, appeared before the court. The case has now been concluded.

Qishuai Company appealed requesting: 1. To vacate the first-instance judgment according to law and revise the judgment to dismiss the claims of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, or to remand for retrial; 2. The court costs of the first and second instance shall be borne entirely by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company.

Grounds of appeal by Qishuai Company: 1. Siemens Company and Siemens China Company initiated the first-instance lawsuit in August 2017, targeting infringing acts before the lawsuit; thus the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC promulgated in 1993 (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) should apply to this case. The first-instance court erred in applying the Anti-Unfair Competition Law amended in 2017. 2. The content of the first-instance judgment is ambiguous, and there is a contradiction between the main text of the judgment and the reasoning part. (1) The same alleged infringing act cannot be simultaneously determined as constituting trademark infringement and unfair competition; (2) The reasoning part of the first-instance judgment determined that Qishuai Company's use of the "SIMBMC" mark constituted trademark infringement, but did not determine that the use of "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." constituted trademark infringement. However, the first item of the main text of the judgment ordered the cessation of the use of "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." but did not order the cessation of the use of the "SIMBMC" mark. 3. Qishuai Company's acts did not infringe the trademark rights of the "SIEMENS" registered trademarks of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company. (1) The "SIMBMC" mark actually used by Qishuai Company's distributors is essentially identical to the "SiMBMC" registered trademark, and the distinctive features are not altered. This act should be resolved by the administrative authority according to law. The first-instance court had no legal basis in substance or procedure to adjudicate this. (2) The vast majority of the marks used by Qishuai Company are the "SiMBMC" registered trademark licensed by a third party. The first-instance court's finding that the alleged infringing products used the "SIMBMC" mark was an error in fact-finding. (3) The alleged infringing mark "SIMBMC" is not similar to the trademark "SIEMENS" under Registration No. G637074 and would not cause confusion among the relevant public. (4) The first-instance court held that Qishuai Company's combined use of the "SiMBMC" registered trademark with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." weakened the distinctiveness of "SIEMENS," thereby constituting an infringing act under Article 57(7) of the Trademark Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law). This was an error in the application of law. 4. Qishuai Company's acts did not constitute unfair competition against the "Siemens" trademark and trade name. (1) Qishuai Company, as authorized, properly indicated the commissioned manufacturer's name "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." on the alleged infringing products. The first-instance court failed to ascertain important facts relating to Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai Siemens Company), and merely because Qishuai Company did not submit other information such as the shareholders of Shanghai Siemens Company, it held that Qishuai Company's defense was unfounded, which was an improper finding of fact. (2) Siemens Company and Siemens China Company do not produce or sell washing machines in China, nor do they use the "Siemens" trademark and trade name on washing machines. Therefore, the trademark and trade name do not have a certain degree of influence and fame among the relevant public for washing machine products. As a result, Qishuai Company's acts would not cause confusion or misidentification among the relevant public. 5. The first-instance court's determination of RMB 100 million in damages lacks basis. (1) The first-instance court, based on multiple news media reports submitted by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, determined Qishuai Company's annual sales at RMB 1.5 billion, and discretionarily determined that the annual sales of products involved in the alleged infringement amounted to one-fifteenth of that, i.e., RMB 100 million, which far exceeds Qishuai Company's actual business situation. (2) The first-instance court, by reference to the profit margins of Qingdao Haier Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haier Company) and Whirlpool (China) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Whirlpool Company), determined the profit margin of the alleged infringing products at 35%, which lacks basis. (3) According to Article 18 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademark Disputes (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation on Application of Law in Trademark Civil Cases), the period of infringement in this case should be calculated at most as two years. The first-instance court discretionarily determined the period of infringement as five years, which is a clear error in fact-finding and misapplication of law. (4) The first-instance court failed to consider the contribution rate of the trademark or trade name to the products when calculating the amount of damages. (5) The damages in this case should be awarded within the statutory limit of RMB 3 million. (6) The first-instance court omitted to consider important facts and circumstances such as Qishuai Company's recall of the alleged infringing products, and the awarded amount was obviously excessive. 6. Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, as shareholders of Qishuai Company, are different legal entities from Qishuai Company. The first-instance court's determination that the two persons should bear joint liability with Qishuai Company constitutes an error in the application of law.

Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong appealed requesting: 1. To vacate the first-instance judgment according to law and revise the judgment to dismiss the claims of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, or to remand for retrial; 2. The court costs of the first and second instance shall be borne entirely by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company.

Grounds of appeal by Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong: 1. During the first-instance proceedings, Siemens Company and Siemens China Company changed their claims several times. In the final amended claim, they did not request Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong to compensate for economic losses. The first-instance court's judgment that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should jointly and severally compensate Siemens Company and Siemens China Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses exceeded the claims of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company and seriously violated legal procedure. 2. The first-instance court found that the property of the shareholders Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, a married couple, was commingled with the company's property, making it equivalent to a one-person limited company, and that the marital relationship implies consistency of intent, giving rise to a common intent to infringe with Qishuai Company, thus constituting joint infringement. The court accordingly held Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong jointly and severally liable for damages. This was an error in fact-finding and lacked legal basis; the judgment should be vacated or remanded for retrial. 3. The first-instance court omitted to consider the fact that Qishuai Company had recalled the alleged infringing products, and thus imposed huge damages, which is unfair. For the above reasons, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong request: 1. To vacate the first-instance judgment according to law and revise the judgment to dismiss the claims of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, or to remand for retrial; 2. The court costs of the first and second instance shall be borne entirely by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company.

Siemens Company and Siemens China Company jointly replied to the appeals of Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong: 1. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law amended in 2017 came into effect on January 1, 2018. The first-instance court docketed the case on January 15, 2019, and the alleged infringing acts were ongoing, with continuing damages. Therefore, the first-instance court's application of the 2017 amendment was proper. 2. Shanghai Siemens Company is merely a shell company incorporated abroad and was used as a tool for infringement by Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong. It is unnecessary to join it as a party to ascertain all facts; it is not a necessary co-party to the litigation. The selection of defendants is the right of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, and Qishuai Company has no right to add defendants. The first-instance court's failure to join Shanghai Siemens Company as a party was proper. 3. The "SIMBMC" trademark used by Qishuai Company imitates and copies the "SIEMENS" trademark under Registration No. G637074. When used together with Chinese names such as "Shanghai Siemens," "Shenzhen Siemens," and "Hong Kong Siemens," it weakens the correlation between "SIEMENS" and Siemens Company, causing confusion among the relevant public. 4. The first-instance court's determination of the amount of damages was correct, with sufficient factual and legal basis. 5. Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several liability with Qishuai Company. (1) Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong are a married couple. As the only two shareholders of Qishuai Company, the company's capital comes from the couple's common property, and the profits are jointly owned. The interests of the couple are highly aligned, and the equity structure of Qishuai Company is singular, making commingling of properties highly likely; it should be considered as a one-person company. (2) Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, as the actual controllers of Qishuai Company, intentionally used Qishuai Company as a platform for infringement. The two persons and Qishuai Company jointly committed the infringing acts, thus they should bear joint tort liability. 6. During the first-instance stage, in the application for amendment of claims submitted to the first-instance court on September 29, 2019, Siemens Company and Siemens China Company inadvertently omitted the claim requesting Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong to bear joint and several liability for damages. However, in the first-instance court hearing, they clearly asserted that the two persons should bear joint and several liability (see page 4 of the hearing record of June 4, 2020). Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong all attended that hearing and presented their defenses, evidence, cross-examination, and arguments on this claim, fully exercising all their rights. Moreover, the complaint and the legal submissions of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company also clearly asserted the joint and several liability of the two persons. Therefore, Siemens Company and Siemens China Company did not waive the claim for their joint liability. 7. The appointment documents submitted by Siemens Company comply with legal requirements. Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong have misunderstood the concepts of "mandatary" and "agent ad litem." In summary, the appeals of Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong should be dismissed.

Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi stated: 1. Siemens China Company has no evidence to prove that Siemens Company licensed it to use the "Siemens" trademark under Registration No. G683480 or the "SIEMENS" trademark under Registration No. G637074. Therefore, Siemens China Company lacks standing to bring a lawsuit for trademark infringement. 2. According to the Interpretation on Application of Law in Trademark Civil Cases, for continuing infringing acts that commenced more than two years before the lawsuit, the amount of damages for infringement shall be calculated retroactively for two years from the date the right holder files the lawsuit with the people's court. The first-instance court discretionarily set the period during which Qishuai Company gained profits from infringement as five years and awarded RMB 100 million, and held that Xinweichuang Company bore joint and several liability within the limit of RMB 500,000, violating the provisions of the above judicial interpretation. 3. Xinweichuang Company had no reason to know that the goods it sold were products infringing the trademark rights in question. According to the Trademark Law, it should not bear liability for damages. Even if it cannot be exempted from liability for damages, it should bear independent liability. The first-instance court's finding that Xinweichuang Company was subjectively at fault and should bear joint and several liability of RMB 500,000 lacks factual and legal basis, and the amount of damages determined was obviously excessive.

Siemens Company and Siemens China Company filed the following claims with the first-instance court: 1. To order the five defendants to immediately cease the acts of infringing the exclusive right to use the trademarks in question and to cease the unfair competition acts infringing the right to use the trade names of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, specifically: to cease using the name "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." on washing machines produced and sold, product packaging, product brochures, contract documents, and internet pages; 2. To order Qishuai Company to compensate Siemens Company and Siemens China Company for economic losses of RMB 100 million and reasonable expenses of RMB 163,000, and to order Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong to bear joint and several liability for the above economic losses and reasonable expenses; and to order Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi to bear joint and several liability within the limit of RMB 3 million; 3. To order Qishuai Company and Xinweichuang Company to publish a public notice in the Legal Daily to eliminate the adverse effects (the notice area shall not be less than 15 x 8 cm); 4. To order the five defendants to bear the court costs.

The first-instance court found the following after trial:

(I) The fame of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company as enterprises, and the fame of the trademarks and products in question

Siemens Company was incorporated in Germany on June 18, 1897. Siemens China Company was incorporated on October 6, 1994, with a registered capital of EUR 900 million, and its business scope includes investment in electrical, electronic, mechanical and other industrial fields, as well as the manufacturing and operation of electrical, electronic, and mechanical products. Since 1993, the two companies have established numerous affiliated enterprises and branches in most major cities in China. From 2009 to 2017, Siemens Company was consistently ranked among the Fortune Global 500, between positions 30 and 71. From 2013 to 2018, "Siemens" was ranked among the top 50 in the Forbes Global Most Valuable Brands list. From 2011 to 2014, Siemens China Company's annual main business revenue exceeded RMB 23 billion, with profits exceeding RMB 5 billion, and it has received numerous awards and honorary titles.

The evidence submitted by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company in the first instance shows that their relevant trademarks were registered early and enjoy high fame. Relevant documents issued by the trademark administrative authority state that the two trademarks in question are designated for use on goods or services in Classes 7, 9, 10, and 11, including "washing machines, machines and equipment for washing and treating laundry" in Class 7. The "Siemens" trademark has been recognized as a well-known trademark on goods in Class 11, such as cabinet-type and chest-type freezers. Additionally, effective judgments of relevant courts have determined that the two trademarks in question have reached the level of well-known marks on controllers in Class 9.

The washing machine products produced by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company are mainly drum-type washing machines with unit prices above RMB 2,000, and they have received numerous industry honors. Multiple pieces of evidence submitted by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company show that Siemens washing machines enjoy considerable product recognition and high market share.

(II) Facts related to the infringement alleged by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company against the five defendants

Shanghai Siemens Company is a company registered in the Republic of Seychelles. Qishuai Company submitted in the litigation a copy of the company's certificate of incorporation and a letter of authorization entrusting Qishuai Company to handle matters related to the 3C certification for washing machine products, but did not submit other information such as the company's shareholders.

The trademark "SiMBMC" under Registration No. 9845563 was applied for registration on August 15, 2011, by Ningbo Free Trade Zone Qunpeng Trading Co., Ltd., and was approved for registration on October 21, 2012, designated for use on goods in Class 7, including "washing machines; dry-cleaning machines; household soymilk makers," among others. The trademark was transferred to Fujishan Electric Appliance Co., Ltd. on May 13, 2016, and later transferred to Cixi Hubin Plastic Spraying Factory on April 6, 2019. During the litigation, Siemens Company filed a request for invalidation against this trademark with the National Intellectual Property Administration, which issued a ruling on April 19, 2021, maintaining the trademark. Siemens Company has filed an administrative lawsuit, which is currently pending.

From March 2017 to August 2018, administrative authorities in Jiangsu, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Henan, Chongqing, Guizhou, Guangxi, Zhejiang and other places successively investigated and dealt with washing machines marked with the labels "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." and "SIMBMC" being sold by relevant vendors on the market. Among them, some administrative authorities determined that the relevant sales conduct infringed the trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. or constituted unfair competition, and issued decisions on penalties, confiscating illegal gains or infringing goods, and imposing fines.

On August 2, 2018, an online article labeled as originating from the Home Appliance Circle, titled "Counterfeit Siemens Washing Machines Withdrawn from Market and Shelves, Whose Alarm Does the Speculator Qishuai Electric Ring?", contained content about Qishuai Company urgently notifying relevant home appliance dealers to stop selling and remove from shelves the entire line of "SIMBMC pulsator washing machines". Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. also submitted multiple reports with similar content. Qishuai Company acknowledged the fact that it recalled some of its products, but did not accept the content in the reports that it was engaging in illegal transactions by riding on the coattails of well-known brands.

On January 1, 2014, Dazhou Evening News reported that local industrial and commercial authorities investigated and dealt with 110 infringing "SIMBMC" washing machines produced by Shanghai Siemens Company, with a total value of over RMB 110,000. This case was rated as one of the top ten typical cases of the "Red Shield Spring Thunder Action" of the Sichuan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce.

On August 13, 2013, the China Enterprise News published a report titled "Siemens Washing Machines Counterfeited Without Knowing?", reporting that the newspaper's reporter, posing as a consumer, called the Qishuai Electric national service hotline and contacted a person claiming to be an authorized dealer of Shanghai Siemens. According to the report, the Shanghai Siemens authorized dealer sent the reporter a company registration certificate of Shanghai Siemens Company and a trademark registration certificate. The reporter saw that Shanghai Siemens Company was registered in Victoria, Republic of Seychelles on April 8, 2012; the so-called "Shanghai Siemens" trademark was the "SIMBMC" trademark registered on October 21, 2012, with the trademark registrant being Ningbo Free Trade Zone Qunpeng Trading Co., Ltd., whose legal representative Qiu Pengjun was also the legal representative of Qishuai Company. The report was reproduced by multiple website platforms.

From August 2013 to April 2014, multiple articles were published on media platforms such as Haoping Home Appliance Network, Home Appliance Consumer Network, Southern Rural News, etc., with content involving Qishuai Company's suspected conduct of riding on the coattails of well-known brands, including by clinging to the "Siemens" brand and other well-known brands. The relevant articles were reproduced on multiple online platforms.

From July 2013 to September 2018, multiple users posted on forum websites such as Baidu Tieba, stating that they had purchased counterfeit Siemens brand washing machines marked with the labels "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." and "SIMBMC".

In the notification of random inspection and testing of commodity quality in the circulation field for the first quarter of 2015 published on the website of the Hunan Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce, and in the random inspection results of washing machines in the circulation field by the Jiangsu Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce in 2016 and 2017, the non-conforming products included washing machines of the "SIMBMC" brand produced by Shanghai Siemens Company.

(3) Facts related to Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd.'s claim of subjective malice and large scale of infringement by the five defendants

In 2003, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong registered and established Hong Kong Siemens Electric Appliances (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Siemens Company) in Hong Kong, with the two being the only shareholders of the company. In 2011, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, as shareholders, invested to establish Fushan Electric Appliances Co., Ltd.

Wang Fugen, the shareholder and legal representative of Shenzhen Jindian Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Siemens Company), together with Wang Qiong, established six enterprises including Shenzhen Qishuai Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Qishuai Company) and Shenzhen Sanling Technology Co., Ltd.

In April 2017, the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce issued an announcement, determining that the washing machine products produced by Qishuai Company and labeled as "Hong Kong Mitsubishi" were defective commodities. Qishuai Company applied for trademarks such as "Philips", "A O Smith", "Fushan and device", "Paike and device" on goods in Class 7 and Class 11. Moreover, the trademark "A O Smith" with application number 3603216, applied for by Qishuai Company, was determined by the Beijing Intellectual Property Court to have not been used for three years, and the court ordered the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce to make a new review decision.

Qishuai Company acknowledged the fact that it was entrusted by Shanghai Siemens Company to handle 3C certification, and directly put the produced washing machine products on the domestic market, while also providing after-sales service for the produced products; Qishuai Company also acknowledged the fact that it was entrusted by Shenzhen Siemens Company to handle 3C certification.

In the QQ space with QQ number 1121445843 and nickname "Dazhou Huimin Electric Appliances", several photos of its physical store selling "SIMBMC" washing machines were displayed, with models mainly being pulsator type, and also a small number of drum type washing machines. The information was posted from September 2014 to September 2016. On e-commerce platforms such as Taobao, JD, and Yihaodian, there were dozens of merchants selling spare parts products for Shanghai Siemens Company washing machines.

According to the introduction on Qishuai Company's website, Qishuai Company was established in 2003, covering an area of over 200 mu (approx. 13.33 hectares), with over 1,000 employees, possessing 6 automated assembly line production equipment and a complete quality inspection center, with an annual production capacity of over 2 million units. On July 8, 2016, the 2016 National Marketing Summit of Qishuai Electric was successfully held at the Pan Pacific Ningbo. Within just 3 hours after the marketing general manager of Qishuai Electric announced the opening policy, Qishuai Electric achieved a contract signing amount of over RMB 300 million, again creating a historic breakthrough. The website promotional content also mentioned that Qishuai Company promoted its brand through CCTV, local media, industry media, and 58,000 terminal distribution outlets nationwide. Qishuai Company was rated by the Cixi Municipal Government as a top 100 enterprise for the period 2013-2018.

Between August and September 2013, media such as NetEase News, Southeast Business Daily, Zhejiang Online, and Phoenix News reported articles about Ningbo Qishuai ranking among the top five washing machine producers in China. The reports mentioned: With the joining of three independent brands, Qisheng, Hanpai, and Shanghai SIMBMC (Shanghai Siemens), Ningbo Qishuai Group, with an annual production capacity of 3 million washing machines, ranked among the top five washing machine manufacturers in China... Company Chairman Gong Yinqi said, "We hope that through the joining of the three brands Qisheng, Hanpai, and Shanghai Siemens, we can provide strong brand support for the sustainable development and growth of the enterprise." In July 2014, Phoenix Finance reported that Gong Yinqi stated that over the past ten years, Qishuai Electric had achieved an annual output value of RMB 1.5 billion, with a 100% growth rate. The channel network of Qishuai Electric had basically no gaps in the domestic market, with thousands of agent customers, building a competitive capability different from other enterprises. On July 20, 2015, China Finance Network reported that the 2015 Marketing Summit of Qishuai Group once again achieved multiple performance breakthroughs, with 1,500 dealers from all over the country participating in the event, achieving a contract signing amount of RMB 420 million in 3 hours. Similar content was reported by platforms such as China Quality News Network and NetEase. Some of the above-mentioned media also reported that Qishuai Company's 2016 Marketing Summit achieved a contract signing amount of RMB 300 million in 3 hours, and in 2017, the order amount in one day reached RMB 320 million. Qishuai Company purchased four industrial land plots locally, with areas of 1.37 hectares, 1 hectare, 1.828 hectares, and 1.505 hectares respectively, and built a second and third factory.

According to the China Compulsory Certification (3C certification) certificates of the China Quality Certification Center, there were multiple certificates where the applicant was Shanghai Siemens Company, the manufacturer was Qishuai Company, and the corresponding products involved nearly 1,400 models of twin-tub washing machines and automatic washing machines, with the certificates valid until August 2018. Hong Kong Siemens Company applied for a 3C certification certificate in October 2012, with the manufacturer being Qishuai Company, involving over 200 models; this certificate was revoked in 2014. Shenzhen Siemens Company applied for a 3C certification certificate in 2018, with the manufacturer being Qishuai Company, involving over 800 models; this certificate is currently valid. The 3C certification certificates involving Qishuai Company as the manufacturer also include those for: Hainan Sanyo Life Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., Samsung (Shanghai) Electric Co., Ltd., Songdian Electric Appliances Nanjing Co., Ltd., Fuji Mountain Electric (Nanjing) Co., Ltd., Hainan Little Swan Water Magic Cube Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., Hong Kong Mitsubishi Electric (Group) Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Wanbao Group Co., Ltd., Panasonic (Shanghai) Electric Co., Ltd., etc., with the products involved all being twin-tub washing machines and automatic washing machines.

In 2014, users posted requirements on Haoyun Logistics Network and Cixi Logistics Network, showing a long-term need for trucks over 9.6 meters from Cixi to Kunshan to carry washing machines, refrigerators, etc., with the contact person being Wu Qianzhi, telephone number 0512-36696620. Through 360 Search, this telephone number was identified as the contact number of Xinweichuang Company.

(4) Information on the five defendants and relevant defense facts of Qishuai Company

Qishuai Company was established on June 11, 2003, with a registered capital of RMB 20 million, as a limited liability company; Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong are shareholders of Qishuai Company, holding 60% and 40% of the shares respectively, and the two are married.

From 2012 to 2019, Qishuai Company entered into contracts or cooperation agreements for advertising, public relations agency, MTV production, communication planning, etc. with Zhongshi Jinqiao International Media Group Co., Ltd., Beijing Shangjieli Cultural Development Center, etc., and invited relevant artists as endorsers. Qishuai Company entered into multiple procurement contracts with companies such as Suning Commerce Group Co., Ltd., Suning Procurement Center, and Xinruimei Electronic Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., involving Qishuai, Hanpai, Paike and other brand washing machines. Qishuai Company also entered into various types of contracts including OEM brand processing contracts, ODM entrusted production processing contracts, brand purchase and sale contracts, OEM and ODM procurement contracts, etc. with more than ten companies including Jinling Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. Qishuai Company registered the "Qishuai" trademark on goods in Class 7. In 2011 and 2017, the Zhejiang Provincial Quality and Technical Supervision Bureau recognized Qishuai Company's Qishuai brand washing machines as Zhejiang famous brand products. During the period from 2015 to 2018, Gong Yinqi, as inventor, and Qishuai Company, as patentee, applied for and obtained 19 utility model patents related to washing machine technology. Qishuai Company submitted relevant invoices, proving that the sales amounts of some brands in 2015, 2016, and 2017 were RMB 12,213,115.71, RMB 15,095,526.28, and RMB 8,714,434.03 respectively; it also submitted a copy of the company registration certificate of Shanghai Siemens Company in the Republic of Seychelles and a letter of entrustment authorizing it to handle 3C certification matters for washing machine products.

Xinweichuang Company was established in May 2013, with a registered capital of RMB 500,000, as a limited liability company (sole proprietorship by a natural person), with the shareholder being Wu Qianzhi; on September 19, 2017, the company type changed to limited liability company (investment or holding by natural persons), and the shareholders changed to Wu Qianzhi and Wang Yali.

(5) Other facts

According to the 2015 and 2016 annual reports released by Haier Company, the gross profit margin of Haier washing machines was 34.33% in 2015 and 34.64% in 2016; according to the 2015 and 2016 annual reports of Whirlpool Company, the gross profit margin of Whirlpool washing machines was 37.49% in 2015 and 37.40% in 2016.

On October 15, 2018, the Ningbo Home Appliances Industry Association issued the "Special Statistical Statement on the Profit Margin of the Washing Machine Industry in Ningbo City", stating therein that from 2013 to 2017, the profit margin of the washing machine industry in Ningbo City ranged from 2.883% to 3.054%.

To claim the reasonable expenses in this case, Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. submitted a lawyer fee invoice of RMB 158,500 and a notarization fee invoice of RMB 14,500.

Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. expressly claimed in this case that the infringing products are limited to those marked with Shanghai Siemens Company.

During the trial, the court of first instance, in accordance with the law, requested Qishuai Company to submit complete financial books of its cooperative business transactions with Shanghai Siemens Company, product production plans, production records (including specific product models and quantities), and its contracts with Xinweichuang Company, as well as complete financial transaction books. At the same time, it requested Xinweichuang Company to submit purchase contracts, sales records, and financial books related to the accused infringing products. Qishuai Company and Xinweichuang Company did not submit them without justifiable reasons.

The court of first instance held that the issues in dispute in this case were: (1) whether the alleged conduct of the five defendants infringed the exclusive right to use registered trademarks of Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. and constituted unfair competition; (2) if so, how the five defendants should bear legal liability.

Because the filing date of this case was before April 2019, and there was no evidence indicating that the infringing conduct of the five defendants continued after April 2019, this case applies the Trademark Law as amended in 2013 and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as revised in 2017.

(1) Whether the alleged infringing conduct constitutes trademark infringement

Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd. claimed that the five defendants constituted trademark infringement based mainly on two aspects: First, the washing machine products produced by Qishuai Company were marked with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd.", with the company name displayed in a bolder font, and the "Siemens" characters used were identical to the "Siemens" trademark of Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd., causing public confusion and misidentification, which fell under the provision of Article 57 of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013: "causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark"; second, Qishuai Company used the "SIMBMC" trademark in combination with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd.", which would lead the public to mistakenly believe that the English equivalent of the Chinese "Siemens" was "SIMBMC", thereby weakening the one-to-one correspondence between the Chinese and English trademarks of Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd.

In this regard, the court of first instance held that, first, in this case, although Qishuai Company used the "Siemens" trademark as a company name on identical goods, it did not prominently use the "Siemens" or "Shanghai Siemens" trade name. Therefore, Qishuai Company's act of marking "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." on washing machine products did not fall under the act of "causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark" as provided in Article 57(7) of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013.

Second, Qishuai Company used the "SIMBMC" mark on washing machine products, which is in the same class of goods as the trademark "SIEMENS" at issue. At the same time, the "SiMBMC" trademark applied for and approved for registration was a combination of letters with a lowercase "i", but the commercial mark used by Qishuai Company on the accused infringing products was "SIMBMC", which is inconsistent with the approved registered trademark. The "i" was changed to an uppercase "I" letter, with a relatively obvious visual difference. This manner of use had already altered the distinctive features of the mark when used as an identifier. From the perspective of ordinary consumers, the above conduct objectively made the "SIMBMC" mark more similar to the "SIEMENS" trademark at issue, easily leading to public confusion or misidentification. Comparing "SIMBMC" with "SIEMENS", both start with the letters "SI" and both have the initial pronunciation "SIM". When consumers see the "SIMBMC" mark used together with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd.", it is obviously easy to mistakenly believe that the "SIMBMC" mark is the English trademark of Siemens Company. Moreover, according to the evidence provided by Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd., there were indeed users who had already been misled in actual scenarios. Qishuai Company's explanation of the "SIMBMC" trademark did not sufficiently account for its design concept or the connection between this choice and the enterprise or related products and services at the level of market operation and value pursuit; it was difficult to consider it reasonable. Therefore, Qishuai Company's act of using "SIMBMC" together with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." weakened the distinctiveness of the "SIEMENS" trademark at issue, falling under the provision of Article 57(7) of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013: "causing other damage to another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark", and constituted trademark infringement.

Finally, Xinweichuang Company, as a professional home appliance product seller, should have had a clear understanding of the well-known status of Siemens Company's trademark at issue. Nonetheless, it still purchased the accused infringing washing machine products from Qishuai Company for resale, showing subjective fault. Therefore, its defense that it had fulfilled its reasonable duty of review and should not bear liability for damages cannot stand, and its act of selling the accused infringing products still constitutes trademark infringement.

(2) Whether the alleged infringing conduct constitutes unfair competition

1. Unfair competition conduct against the company names of Siemens AG and Siemens China Co., Ltd.

Article 6(2) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as revised in 2017 provides that business operators shall not engage in the following confusing conduct that leads people to mistake their goods for those of others or to believe there is a specific connection with others: ... (2) unauthorized use of another person's enterprise name (including abbreviation, trade name, etc.) that has certain influence, social organization name (including abbreviation, etc.), or name (including pseudonym, stage name, translated name, etc.); ...

In the present case, the established facts indicate that the joint trade name "Siemens" of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China has a certain degree of influence, and their respective enterprise names also constitute enterprise names with certain influence. The act of Qishuai Company in labeling the washing machine products with the name "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." constitutes the unauthorized use of another person's enterprise name with certain influence, thereby constituting unfair competition. Although Qishuai Company argued that its use of the Shanghai Siemens Company's name was for the production of the allegedly infringing washing machine products under the entrustment of Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., a comprehensive review of all evidence in the case reveals that this defense of Qishuai Company cannot stand. The reasons are as follows: First, "Siemens," as an enterprise name, enjoys very high renown. As a professional washing machine manufacturer, Qishuai Company could not have been unaware of the renown of the enterprise names of Siemens-related companies. Nevertheless, it still accepted the entrustment of Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. to produce washing machines. Moreover, after the lawsuit was initiated, apart from submitting a copy of the business registration certificate of Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., it was unable to submit any other evidentiary materials related to the entity of Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., which is evidently contrary to the general understanding of business operations in the commercial field. Second, from the process of Qishuai Company's production of the allegedly infringing products, aside from a copy of the company registration certificate from the Republic of Seychelles, Qishuai Company was responsible for all processes from the application for 3C certification, production, sales, to after-sales service of the allegedly infringing products. It can be said that, except for the nominal entrustment by Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., all actual procedures of certification, production, sales, and after-sales service for the allegedly infringing products were handled by Qishuai Company. Under such circumstances, Qishuai Company's inability to submit any evidence such as entrustment contracts, production contracts, or fund settlement certificates with Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. is clearly inconsistent with common sense. Third, from the past conduct of Gong Yinqi, the actual controller of Qishuai Company, and Wang Qiong, it can be observed that, despite having no connection whatsoever with Siemens AG or Siemens Ltd., China, they established the Hong Kong Siemens Company in 2003, using "Siemens" as the trade name, demonstrating a clear subjective intent to leverage the renown of the enterprise names of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. Wang Qiong also jointly established Shenzhen Qishuai Company with Wang Fugen, the legal representative of Shenzhen Siemens Company. Fourth, Qishuai Company's act of labeling the allegedly infringing products with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." is likely to cause confusion or misidentification among consumers, leading them to believe that Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd. is affiliated with Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, and consequently to mistakenly believe that the allegedly infringing products are the products of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, or have a specific connection therewith. In summary, the court of first instance found that the alleged infringing act of Qishuai Company, subjectively, exhibited the intent to leverage the goodwill of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, and objectively, was likely to cause consumer misidentification, thereby constituting unfair competition.

Xinweichuang Company, as a professional distributor of home appliance products, clearly should have had a clear understanding of the renown of "Siemens" as an enterprise name. However, it still purchased washing machine products labeled with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." from Qishuai Company for sale, subjectively being at fault, and objectively selling products that use another person's enterprise name with certain influence without authorization. Its conduct also constitutes unfair competition.

2. Unfair Competitive Conduct Regarding the Trademarks Involved

Pursuant to Article 58 of the Trademark Law (amended in 2013), using another person's registered trademark or unregistered well-known mark as a trade name in an enterprise name, thereby misleading the public, constitutes an act of unfair competition, and shall be dealt with in accordance with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law (revised in 2017). In this case, "Siemens" is not only the trade name of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China but also a registered trademark. Qishuai Company's act of labeling the allegedly infringing products with an enterprise name containing the registered trademarks of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, misleading the public, falls under the category of "other confusing acts sufficient to cause people to mistakenly believe that the goods are those of another person or have a specific connection with another person" as stipulated in Item (4) of Article 6 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law (revised in 2017), thereby constituting unfair competition. As also stated above, Xinweichuang Company was subjectively at fault, and its sale of the allegedly infringing products also constitutes an act of unfair competition.

(3) How the Civil Liability of the Five Defendants Should Be Borne

Qishuai Company and Xinweichuang Company committed trademark infringement and unfair competition acts and shall bear corresponding civil liability.

1. Regarding the Civil Liability to Be Borne by Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong

First, regarding the specific amount of damages. The court of first instance held that the claim of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China to calculate Qishuai Company's profits from the infringing products and acts based on the annual sales revenue of RMB 1.5 billion as reported in news articles was inappropriate. This is because Qishuai Company did not only produce the "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." brand of washing machines. The proportion of sales revenue from the specific infringing products within its total sales revenue is unclear, and the profits from the trademark infringement and the unfair competition acts cannot be clearly distinguished. Therefore, since both the losses suffered by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China due to the infringement and the profits gained by Qishuai Company from the infringement cannot be determined, the relevant compensation liability shall be reasonably analyzed and comprehensively determined by giving full consideration to the rights status of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, the subjective state and objective conduct of Qishuai Company in committing the alleged infringing acts, based on the evidence on record and the facts found. The following factors shall be given particular consideration:

(1) The renown of the Siemens trademark and enterprise name. As a Fortune Global 500 company and with the Siemens brand as one of the world's top 100 brands, the renown of its trademark and enterprise name is extremely high. (2) The subjective malice of Qishuai Company's infringement. As previously mentioned, although Qishuai Company argued that it produced the allegedly infringing washing machines under the entrustment of Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., its defense was inconsistent with common sense and the general understanding in the market operation field in many respects. Moreover, considering a series of facts, including the establishment of the Hong Kong Siemens Company by Qishuai Company's actual controller Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong in 2003, Qishuai Company's applications for registration of trademarks such as "Philips" and "A O Smith," Qishuai Company's acceptance of 3C certification entrustment from Shenzhen Siemens Company, and the fact that Shenzhen Qishuai Company was jointly established by Wang Qiong and the legal representative of Shenzhen Siemens Company, it is evident that Qishuai Company subjectively had the clear intent to leverage the goodwill of well-known enterprises. (3) The scale of Qishuai Company's infringement. Based on the evidence submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China and some of Qishuai Company's promotional materials, the scale of Qishuai Company's production and sales is substantial. Its promotional materials claim annual sales revenue of RMB 1.5 billion, and its marketing summits from 2015 to 2017 each achieved signing amounts of RMB 300 million to RMB 400 million within a few hours. Although these amounts cannot be deemed to be all sales revenue from the allegedly infringing products, they can serve as a reference for determining the amount of damages. Although Qishuai Company submitted evidence proving its sales revenue of some other brands from 2015 to 2017, the total amount represented by the invoices it submitted does not exceed RMB 15 million, which is far from the claimed RMB 1.5 billion in sales revenue. From the investigation results of market supervision and administration departments across various regions, it can be seen that the sales scope of Qishuai Company's washing machines labeled with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." is very broad, covering most provinces and municipalities directly under the central government across the country, including Sichuan, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Henan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Chongqing. At the same time, Qishuai Company claimed that it has over 1,500 dealers nationwide, with terminal distribution points reaching 58,000, further demonstrating the broad sales scope of its products. From the number of product models covered by the 3C certification certificates applied for by Qishuai Company, it can be seen that it produces a large number of product models. Although Qishuai Company argued that many of the applied models were not actually produced, even if only half of the models were actually produced, there would still be over 700 different product models. (4) The duration of Qishuai Company's infringement. From news reports and other supporting evidence submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, it can be seen that Qishuai Company's use of the name "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." for the production and sale of washing machines lasted at least from 2013 to 2018, a period of five years. (5) The profit margin of washing machine products. Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China submitted the annual reports of Haier Group and Whirlpool Corporation, which show that the gross profit margin of washing machine products is between 34% and 37%. Since the relevant data in the annual reports of listed companies are audited by professional accounting departments, these figures are highly reliable. Although Qishuai Company submitted a statement on industry profit margins issued by the Ningbo Household Appliances Industry Association, the association does not have professional financial audit capabilities, nor did it submit the specific sources of the data in the statement. Therefore, the industry profit margin in that statement is not admissible. (6) During the trial of the first instance, the court clearly required Qishuai Company to submit its complete financial account books for its business dealings with Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd., production plans, production records, as well as its contracts and complete financial transaction account books with Xinweichuang Company. Under circumstances where Qishuai Company should have possessed or held the relevant contracts and account books, it clearly had the conditions to provide evidence and possessed the relevant evidence, but it refused to submit the above materials. (7) The reasonable expenses incurred by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China for enforcing their rights. Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China submitted invoices for legal fees of RMB 158,500 and notarization fees of RMB 14,500. However, in their complaint, they only claimed reasonable expenses of RMB 163,000. This claimed amount is lower than the total invoice amount, which should be deemed as Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China waiving their claim for the remaining reasonable expenses.

In summary, the court of first instance determined the amount of damages with reference to the claims and evidence submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. Based on multiple news reports submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, the annual sales revenue of Qishuai Company was determined to be RMB 1.5 billion; based on evidence such as OEM contracts signed by Qishuai Company with other companies, the annual sales revenue of Qishuai Company relating to the allegedly infringing products was determined to be one-fifteenth of RMB 1.5 billion, i.e., RMB 100 million; the profit margin for the allegedly infringing products was determined to be 35% by reference to the profit margins disclosed by Haier Group and Whirlpool Corporation; the duration of the infringement was determined to be five years. Accordingly, Qishuai Company's profit from the infringement is at least RMB 100,000,000 × 35% × 5 = RMB 175,000,000, which is far higher than the RMB 100 million in damages claimed by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. Therefore, the court of first instance upheld the damage claim of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China in full. At the same time, the reasonable expenses of RMB 163,000 incurred by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China for enforcing their rights were also upheld in full.

Second, regarding whether Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several liability. The court of first instance held that, on the one hand, the shareholders of Qishuai Company are Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, who are married. In terms of property attributes, this can be regarded as equivalent to a one-person limited liability company. Where Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong fail to submit evidence proving that their marital property is independent from the company's property, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong shall be jointly and severally liable for the debts of Qishuai Company. On the other hand, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, based on their marital relationship, share unity of intent. Considering the circumstances such as Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong establishing the Hong Kong Siemens Company, applying for the "SiMBMC" trademark through other companies, and Wang Qiong jointly establishing Shenzhen Qishuai Company with the legal representative of Shenzhen Siemens Company, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong are also the actual controllers of Qishuai Company. Their intent to infringe as natural persons is evident, and they played an important role in the implementation of the infringement acts under the guise of the company. They should be deemed to have shared the intent for joint infringement with Qishuai Company, constituting joint infringement. In summary, Gong Yinqi, Wang Qiong, and Qishuai Company shall bear joint and several liability for damages in this case.

2. Regarding the Civil Liability to Be Borne by Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi

Since Xinweichuang Company was subjectively at fault, even though it was only a reseller, it shall still bear partial joint and several liability with Qishuai Company within the scope of its sale of the infringing products. Based on the quantity of infringing products seized from Xinweichuang Company and the information on logistics needs posted on the internet by Wu Qianzhi, the court of first instance determined that Xinweichuang Company shall bear joint and several liability with Qishuai Company for damages up to RMB 500,000.

Article 63 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2013) (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law) provides that where a shareholder of a one-person limited liability company cannot prove that the company's property is independent from the shareholder's own property, the shareholder shall be jointly and severally liable for the company's debts. At the time the infringing products were discovered at Xinweichuang Company, Xinweichuang Company was a limited liability company with Wu Qianzhi as its sole shareholder. Wu Qianzhi also failed to submit evidence proving that Xinweichuang Company's property was independent from his personal property. Therefore, he shall be jointly and severally liable for the debts of Xinweichuang Company.

3. Regarding Elimination of Adverse Effects

Qishuai Company's production and sale of washing machine products labeled with "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." lasted for a long time, covered a wide sales scope, and has already caused misidentification among ordinary consumers, adversely affecting the distinctiveness of the trademarks and goodwill of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. Therefore, the claim of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China that Qishuai Company be ordered to publish an announcement in relevant newspapers or media to eliminate the adverse effects has factual and legal basis and should be upheld. The announcement of Qishuai Company shall clearly state that the identifiers "SIMBMC" and "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." have no connection whatsoever with Siemens AG or Siemens Ltd., China, and that the products produced by Qishuai Company bearing the above two identifiers also have no connection whatsoever with Siemens AG or Siemens Ltd., China. Since the publication of an announcement by Qishuai Company is sufficient to eliminate the adverse effects, the claim of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China that Xinweichuang Company also be ordered to publish an announcement is no longer upheld.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Articles 57, 58, and 63 of the Trademark Law (amended in 2013), Articles 6 and 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law (revised in 2017), Article 63 of the Company Law (amended in 2013), Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Trademarks, Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Cases Involving Conflicts between Registered Trademarks, Enterprise Names and Prior Rights, and Article 145 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Xinweichuang Company and Qishuai Company shall immediately cease the acts of infringing the exclusive rights to the trademarks involved and the acts of unfair competition, i.e., cease using the name "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliances Co., Ltd." on the washing machines they produce and sell, product packaging, product brochures, contract documents, and internet pages; 2. Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong shall, within thirty days from the date the judgment takes effect, jointly and severally compensate Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China for economic losses of RMB 100,000,000 and reasonable expenses of RMB 163,000; Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi shall bear joint and several liability for the above amount up to RMB 500,000; 3. Qishuai Company shall, within thirty days from the date the judgment takes effect, publish an announcement in the Legal Daily to eliminate the adverse effects (the content shall be subject to review by the court of first instance); if it fails to publish within the time limit, the court of first instance shall select a media outlet to publish the content of the judgment, and the costs shall be borne by Qishuai Company; 4. The other claims of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China are rejected. The case acceptance fee of RMB 542,615 shall be borne by Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong in the amount of RMB 533,815, and by Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi in the amount of RMB 8,800.

After this Court accepted the case for second instance, it served the Notice of Submission of Evidence for the Second Instance on all parties, clearly informing each party that they should submit evidence to this Court within 10 days from the day following receipt of the notice. Evidence materials submitted beyond the time limit shall not be organized for cross-examination during the trial, unless the opposing party agrees to cross-examination.

Qishuai Company received the Notice of Submission of Evidence on August 30, 2022. Thereafter, on October 26, November 10, December 7, 2022, and January 9, 2023, respectively, it submitted four groups of evidence to this Court, totaling 22 pieces of evidence, to prove that the amount of damages determined by the judgment of first instance was excessively high.

Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China argued that the evidence submitted by Qishuai Company exceeded the time limit for evidence submission specified by the court and therefore did not consent to cross-examination. They also argued that the above evidence does not constitute new evidence for the second instance and should not be included in the scope of the second instance trial, and that the content of the evidence cannot prove Qishuai Company's claims.

Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi also submitted 13 pieces of evidence to this Court during the second instance stage, the content of which was essentially consistent with what Qishuai Company intended to prove with its corresponding evidence.

Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China also refused to consent to cross-examination on the grounds that the evidence submitted by Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi exceeded the time limit for evidence submission. At the same time, they argued that the above evidence materials were essentially the same as those submitted by Qishuai Company, and that Xinweichuang Company, as a reseller, had formed an offensive and defensive alliance with the manufacturer during the litigation, intentionally or under instruction helping the manufacturer to evade liability, constituting an act of bad faith in litigation.

With respect to the above evidence, this Court holds that the relevant evidence cannot prove Qishuai Company's claims. Moreover, the timing of Qishuai Company's submission of the evidence materials far exceeded the time limit for evidence submission specified by this Court. Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China have also clearly expressed their refusal to consent to cross-examination. Therefore, this Court does not admit the evidence submitted by Qishuai Company. Since Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi did not file an appeal, and the evidence materials they submitted are directed at Qishuai Company's claims, this Court also does not admit the evidence materials submitted by Xinweichuang Company and Wu Qianzhi.

During the proceedings of the second instance, Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, Wang Qiong, Xinweichuang Company, and Wu Qianzhi all raised objections to this Court, arguing that Siemens AG did not affix its seal to the civil complaint, that its authorized representative did not have the qualification to act as a litigation representative, and that the act of signing the complaint was invalid, meaning that Siemens AG should be deemed not to have initiated the lawsuit; even if it were considered that the above-mentioned authorized representative had the qualification of a representative, that representative did not appear in court to participate in the litigation, and the case should be treated as having been withdrawn by default.

This Court examined the objections raised by the above parties concerning the procedure of Siemens AG's authorized representative and the company's qualification as a litigant. Upon review, it is found that the acts of Siemens AG in appointing an authorized representative and its entrusted litigation representative complied with the procedures and conditions stipulated in the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The company has the qualification as a litigant; its entrusted litigation representative also has the qualification as a participant in the litigation and has the right to exercise the corresponding litigation rights in this case.

This Court has determined through trial that among the English identifiers used by Qishuai Company on the allegedly infringing products, outer packaging, and promotional materials, some are "SIMBMC" and some are "SiMBMC." The court of first instance found that all English identifiers used in the alleged infringing acts were "SIMBMC," which is an error of fact. This Court hereby points this out. The other facts found by the court of first instance are true and are confirmed by this Court.

The Court further finds that Qishuai Company clearly stated during the second-instance trial that the accused infringing products were manufactured for its own needs and not upon another party's commission; its use of the mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." on the accused infringing products and in its business activities was based on its multi-brand strategy; and Fan Liudan, the legal representative of Shanghai Siemens Company, was an employee of Qishuai Company and paid social insurance by Qishuai Company.

It is further found that the Beijing Intellectual Property Court, on April 19, 2023, rendered Administrative Judgment No. (2021) Jing 73 Xing Chu 14416, holding that the registration of Trademark No. 9845563 "SiMBMC" constituted the circumstances under Article 13(2) and Article 41(1) of the Trademark Law as amended in 2001 and should be declared invalid, and set aside the ruling of the National Intellectual Property Administration upholding the validity of the trademark registration, ordering the National Intellectual Property Administration to issue a new ruling. Both the holder of the trademark, Cixi Hubin Plastic Spray Co., Ltd., and the National Intellectual Property Administration appealed against the said judgment, and the case is currently under second-instance trial.

Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China stated during the second-instance trial that the amount of damages claimed in this case does not include compensation for trademark infringement, i.e., they do not seek compensation for the trademark infringement part and will not file a separate action for compensation for the trademark infringement involved in this case in the future; in addition, they also did not request the cessation of use of the accused infringing marks "SiMBMC" and "SIMBMC" in this case.

The above facts are confirmed by the evidence on file at first instance, the statements of the parties during the second-instance trial, and relevant legal instruments.

The Court holds that, in light of the appeals and defenses of the parties, the issues in dispute at second instance are as follows: (1) whether the first-instance court correctly applied the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 to this case; (2) whether the accused acts of Qishuai Company infringed the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China; (3) whether the accused acts of Qishuai Company constituted unfair competition against Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China; (4) whether the amount of damages determined by the first-instance court is appropriate; and (5) whether the first-instance court correctly held Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong jointly and severally liable with Qishuai Company for damages.

(1) Regarding the issue of whether the application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 is correct in this case.

Upon investigation, Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China first initiated the lawsuit in August 2017, which is earlier than the effective date of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 (January 1, 2018). However, the evidence submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China shows that the accused infringing acts continued after January 1, 2018. Therefore, the first-instance court's application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 to this case was not improper. Qishuai Company's contention that the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 1993 should apply and that the first-instance court erred in applying the law cannot be sustained.

(2) Regarding the issue of whether the accused acts of Qishuai Company infringed the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China.

In this case, based on the claims of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China and the evidence on file, the accused infringing marks used by Qishuai Company on the accused infringing products, product packaging, and related promotional activities include "SiMBMC," "SIMBMC," and "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd."

1. Concerning the accused infringing marks "SiMBMC" and "SIMBMC"

Given that Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China have expressly stated that they do not seek compensation for the trademark infringement involved in this case and will not file a separate action for compensation in the future, and that they also did not request the cessation of use of the accused infringing marks "SiMBMC" and "SIMBMC," it is evident that Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China have no specific claim regarding Qishuai Company's use of "SiMBMC" and "SIMBMC." Therefore, the Court does not address whether this part of the acts infringed the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China.

2. Concerning the issue of whether Qishuai Company's use of the accused infringing mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." infringed the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China.

Qishuai Company's use of the mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." in this case can be divided into three scenarios: first, use on the bodies of washing machines; second, use on the outer packaging of washing machines; and third, use in promotional activities. The Court analyzes and assesses each scenario separately.

(1) Use on the bodies of washing machines. First, the mark is placed in a prominent position on the machine panel, and relevant consumers are likely to perceive it as an indicator of product source, thus constituting trademark use. Although Qishuai Company claims that the mark is the company name of a third party and that it is authorized to use that company name, based on the facts found by the Court, the accused infringing products were manufactured by Qishuai Company for its own development. Generally, it is unusual for an enterprise to prominently affix another party's company name on its own products. Moreover, according to Qishuai Company's statements during the second-instance trial, its use of the mark was part of a multi-brand strategy, indicating that the original intention was to use the mark as a trademark rather than as a company name. Second, Qishuai Company's use of the mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." on washing machine bodies falls within the same category of goods as the goods for which the trademark "Siemens" (西门子) is registered under Class 7 (washing machines). Third, in the mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd.," "Shanghai" is a geographic indicator, and "Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." is a term indicating the nature and form of the commercial entity; neither is distinctive. However, "Siemens" (西门子) is highly distinctive and identifiable, constituting the distinctive part of the mark. This part is identical to the trademark "Siemens" (西门子) at issue. Therefore, the mark as a whole is similar to the trademark at issue. In conclusion, Qishuai Company's use of "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." as a whole as a trademark on washing machine bodies, being similar to the trademark at issue, is likely to cause confusion or misidentification among relevant consumers. This act falls under the circumstance described in Article 57(2) of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013: "using a trademark similar to the registered trademark on the same kind of goods without the authorization of the trademark registrant, which is likely to cause confusion." Such act infringes the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China.

(2) Use on product outer packaging and in promotional activities. Typically, manufacturers affix their company names on product outer packaging and in promotional activities. In this case, Qishuai Company stated that the accused infringing products were its own products, that it accepted a commission from the third party Shanghai Siemens Company to apply for 3C certification for the accused infringing products, and that it was authorized to use the company name. There is a considerable discrepancy between Qishuai Company's statements above and its claims at first instance and its grounds of appeal. However, since affixing a company name on product outer packaging and in promotional activities is a normal commercial practice, the Court may accept its claim that it used another party's company name. According to Article 58 of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013, using another party's registered trademark or unregistered well-known trademark as a part of a company name, thereby misleading the public and constituting unfair competition, shall be dealt with under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Therefore, Qishuai Company's accused act falls under the circumstances described in the above legal provision and shall be dealt with under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, as discussed below.

In summary, Qishuai Company's use of "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." on the bodies of the accused infringing products infringes the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. The first-instance court erred in its factual findings and application of law on this point, and the Court rectifies this.

(3) Regarding the issue of whether the accused acts of Qishuai Company constitute unfair competition against Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China.

Article 58 of the Trademark Law as amended in 2013 provides that using another party's registered trademark as a part of a company name, thereby misleading the public and constituting unfair competition, shall be dealt with under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Article 6 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 provides that a business operator shall not engage in the following confusing acts that cause others to mistake the goods for the goods of another party or to believe that there is a specific connection with another party: ... (2) without authorization, using another party's enterprise name with certain influence (including abbreviations, trade names, etc.), social organization name (including abbreviations, etc.), or personal name (including pen name, stage name, translated name, etc.) ... (4) other confusing acts sufficient to cause others to mistake the goods for the goods of another party or to believe that there is a specific connection with another party. Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a business operator engages in any of the following confusing acts, sufficient to cause others to mistake the goods for the goods of another party or to believe that there is a specific connection with another party, the people's court may find it to constitute unfair competition under Article 6(4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law: ... (2) using another party's registered trademark or unregistered well-known trademark as a part of a company name, thereby misleading the public.

In this case, based on the facts found, Siemens AG was established in 1897, over 120 years ago; Siemens Ltd., China was established in 1994 and its investment scope in China includes the electrical, electronic, and mechanical industries, with numerous affiliated companies and branches. For many years after 2011, Siemens Ltd., China's main business revenue exceeded RMB 20 billion; from 2009 to 2017, Siemens AG was ranked among the Fortune Global 500; in 2013, the Siemens brand was ranked 35th on the list of the world's most valuable brands, with a value of US$13.7 billion; Siemens drum washing machines received numerous honors and achieved the second largest market share as early as 2006. The above facts all demonstrate that the trade name "Siemens" (西门子) of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China has certain influence, and their company names are also company names with certain influence.
