In addition, the Chinese and English trademarks of Siemens were registered in China as early as 1997 and 1995, and the Trademark Office of the former State Administration for Industry and Commerce and courts have found the Chinese and English trademarks of Siemens to be well-known in Class 9 and Class 11 goods in previous rulings or judgments. Qishuai Company's use of the company name "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." on the outer packaging of the accused infringing products and in promotional activities, because the trade name "Siemens" (西门子) in that company name is identical to the trade name of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China and their registered Chinese trademark "Siemens" (西门子), is likely to cause relevant consumers to mistake the accused infringing products for products of Siemens AG or Siemens Ltd., China, or to believe that there is an affiliation with them. Therefore, its act constitutes using without authorization another party's company name with certain influence and using another party's registered trademark as a part of a company name, falling under the circumstances described in Article 6(2) and (4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017, and thus constitutes unfair competition.

Qishuai Company argues that its use of the company name "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." was authorized by Shanghai Siemens Company and is a proper use of a company name. In this regard, the Court holds that whether Qishuai Company obtained authorization to use the company name does not affect the determination and handling of the act as unfair competition. Furthermore, Shanghai Siemens Company is an offshore registered company. Qishuai Company claims that it was lawfully authorized to use that company name, but apart from submitting a registration certificate and a letter of authorization for Shanghai Siemens Company, it failed to submit any other evidence relating to the status of Shanghai Siemens Company or any written contract between it and Shanghai Siemens Company. This is both inconsistent with common sense and lacks sufficient factual basis. Even if Qishuai Company's statements were true, given that the company names and registered trademarks of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China are highly well-known, Qishuai Company, as a professional washing machine manufacturer, should have been aware of the relevant circumstances. In such circumstances, its acceptance of authorization from Shanghai Siemens Company to affix the company name of Shanghai Siemens Company on washing machine products, product outer packaging, and in promotional activities cannot be considered bona fide. In addition, looking at the past conduct of Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong, shareholders of Qishuai Company, they established Hong Kong Siemens Company (香港西门子公司) in Hong Kong in 2003 using "Siemens" (西门子) as a trade name and produced and sold products bearing that company name, despite having no connection with Siemens AG or Siemens Ltd., China. This also demonstrates Qishuai Company's obvious intent to free-ride on the goodwill of others. Therefore, the Court does not support Qishuai Company's relevant appeal arguments.

Furthermore, Qishuai Company argues that the same accused infringing act cannot be both an infringement of trademark rights and unfair competition, and that the first-instance court erred in law by not distinguishing between the cessation of trademark infringement and unfair competition and by rendering a mixed judgment. The Court holds that Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China enjoy trademark rights over their registered trademark "Siemens" (西门子) and company name rights over their trade name "Siemens" (西门子). Qishuai Company's use of the accused infringing mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." in different scenarios infringes both the trademark rights and the company name rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China. Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China have pursued Qishuai Company's corresponding legal liability under the Trademark Law as amended in 2013 and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017, respectively. It is not improper for the people's court to make separate determinations accordingly. Although the first-instance court erred in failing to find that Qishuai Company's separate use of "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." constituted infringement of the registered trademark rights of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, since both the trademark infringement and unfair competition in this case manifest as the use of the said mark, the first-instance court's main judgment item 1, which orders Xinweichuang Company and Qishuai Company to immediately cease the infringement of the trademark rights involved and the unfair competition, i.e., to cease using the mark "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd.," was not improper.

(4) Regarding the issue of whether the amount of damages determined by the first-instance court is appropriate.

Given that during the second-instance stage, Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China clarified that they only seek compensation for the unfair competition part and not for the trademark infringement part, the Court will determine the damages solely for Qishuai Company's unfair competition act.

Article 17(3) and (4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017 provide: "The amount of damages for an operator damaged by an act of unfair competition shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the operator due to the infringement; where the actual losses are difficult to calculate, it shall be determined based on the benefits gained by the infringer from the infringement. The amount of damages shall also include the reasonable expenses paid by the operator to stop the infringement. Where the operator violates Article 6 or Article 9 of this Law, and the actual losses of the right holder due to the infringement or the benefits gained by the infringer from the infringement are difficult to determine, the people's court may, based on the circumstances of the infringement, award damages of not more than RMB 3 million to the right holder."

In this case, Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China claim that the damages should be calculated based on the benefits gained by Qishuai Company from the infringement. The Court holds that the benefits gained by Qishuai Company from the infringement refer to the benefits obtained by Qishuai Company from the production and sale of the accused infringing products during the alleged infringement period. Given that Qishuai Company also produces and sells products under other brands besides the accused infringing products, the benefits from production and sale not related to the accused infringing products should be deducted from the total benefits when calculating the infringement benefits. Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, apart from submitting relevant news reports as a basis for determining the damages, failed to provide other evidence capable of proving the infringement benefits of Qishuai Company. Since the content of the said news reports is the total annual sales of Qishuai Company and cannot distinguish the proportion of sales of the accused infringing products in the total sales, the evidence is insufficient to determine the infringement benefits of Qishuai Company.

Based on the available evidence: First, from the promotional materials of Qishuai Company submitted by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, it is known that Qishuai Company's production and sales scale is huge; multiple news reports show that Qishuai Company's annual sales amount to RMB 1.5 billion. Among them, the signing amounts at the marketing summits from 2015 to 2017 each reached RMB 300-400 million within several hours. Second, from the investigations by local market supervision and management departments, it can be seen that the sales scope of Qishuai Company's washing machine products marked with "Shanghai Siemens Electrical Appliances Co., Ltd." is very wide, covering most provinces and municipalities directly under the central government in China, such as Sichuan, Jiangsu, Shaanxi, Hunan, Yunnan, Henan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Chongqing. At the same time, Qishuai Company claims that it has over 1,500 dealers nationwide and 58,000 terminal sales outlets, further proving the wide sales scope of its products. Third, from the number of product models covered by Qishuai Company's 3C certification applications, it can be seen that the accused infringing products produced by it have many models and a large quantity. The above circumstances, combined with factors such as the profit rate of the washing machine industry, allow the Court to find that the benefits gained by Qishuai Company from the production and sale of the accused infringing products clearly exceed the statutory maximum damages of RMB 3 million provided in Article 17(4) of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law as amended in 2017. In such circumstances, taking into account the high reputation of the company names of Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China, Qishuai Company's obvious subjective bad faith, the large scale and long duration of the infringement, and considering the profit rate of washing machine products and the reasonable expenses incurred by Siemens AG and Siemens Ltd., China to protect their rights, the damages in this case should be determined above the statutory maximum. The first-instance court, in the absence of Qishuai Company's submission of relevant financial evidence, used the media report content on file as the basis for calculating total sales, and calculated the proportion of sales of the accused infringing products as one-fifteenth. On the basis of integrating relevant case factors, the first-instance court's discretion to determine the damages amount above the statutory maximum was not improper.

Qishuai Company argued: 1. The court of first instance determined that Qishuai Company's annual sales were RMB 1.5 billion based on the company's website promotional materials, which lacked a factual basis. The calculation of the sales volume of the accused infringing products and the resulting determination of the amount of damages also lacked a basis. 2. The business structures, company scales, and pricing strategies of Haier Company and Whirlpool Company were different from those of Qishuai Company, and the profit margins of those companies should not be used to determine the profit margin of the accused infringing products. 3. Qishuai Company had a small production scale, which was far from the situation reflected by the evidence submitted by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company. This Court is of the opinion that: First, although Qishuai Company claimed that the evidence submitted by Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, such as the website promotional materials, was inconsistent with the facts, it clearly stated at the second-instance trial that it had not raised any objection, issued any clarification, or resorted to legal channels to address such false reports. Moreover, when this Court expressly requested Qishuai Company to submit relevant evidence, it still failed to submit financial ledgers or other evidence related to the accused infringing products. In the absence of other evidence to prove Qishuai Company's profits from the infringement, it was not improper for the People's Court to refer to the aforementioned media reports to determine the amount of damages. Second, Siemens Company, Haier Company, and Whirlpool Company are all leading enterprises in the production of washing machines. In determining the amount of damages to be paid to Siemens Company and Siemens China Company in this case, the profit margins of the above two companies had strong reference value. Moreover, the gross profit margins of washing machine products reflected in the annual reports of those two companies were merely a reference factor for determining the damages in this case and were not the sole basis for the determination. The court of first instance had already comprehensively considered the actual circumstances of the case and made an estimate and adjustment in its determination. Third, the evidence on record was insufficient to support Qishuai Company's claims regarding its small production scale and low profit margins. Therefore, this Court does not adopt the above claims of Qishuai Company.

It should be noted that, although Siemens Company and Siemens China Company clearly stated at the second-instance trial that the amount of damages they claimed did not include damages for trademark infringement, in this case both the trademark infringement and the unfair competition were manifested in the use of the accused infringing mark "Shanghai Siemens Electric Appliance Co., Ltd." The profits were also derived from the production and marketing of the accused infringing products. The production and sales volume of the accused infringing products was fixed. Furthermore, according to the aforementioned method for determining damages, even considering only the unfair competition aspect, the determination of RMB 100 million in damages was not manifestly improper. Therefore, this Court affirms the amount of damages determined by the court of first instance.

(V) Whether the court of first instance correctly ordered Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong to bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company

First, whether the court of first instance's judgment that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong bear joint and several compensatory liability exceeded the claims. Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong appealed, arguing that Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, in their last amended Statement of Claim submitted on September 29, 2019, did not claim that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company, and thus the judgment of the court of first instance exceeded the claims. Upon review, it was found that Siemens Company and Siemens China Company had indeed amended their claims multiple times during the first-instance proceedings. In the Civil Statement of Claim for Amended Claims submitted on August 1, 2019, they stated that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company. In the Statement of Claim for Amended Claims submitted on September 29, 2019, they did not claim that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company. However, their authorized litigation representatives clearly stated in the court hearing organized by the court of first instance on June 4, 2020, that they claimed Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company. None of the parties raised any objection to this, and they all submitted corresponding defense responses to this claim. Accordingly, this should be regarded as the final claim of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability in this case. The court of first instance's review and judgment on this matter did not exceed the scope of the claims and was not improper.

Second, whether Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company. According to the facts already ascertained in this case, Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong are the only two shareholders of Qishuai Company. As the actual controllers of Qishuai Company, these two individuals played a significant role in the implementation of the infringing acts by Qishuai Company. Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong had previously established Hong Kong Siemens Company in Hong Kong in 2003 using "Siemens" as the trade name. They also applied for the registration of the "SiMBMC" trademark through other companies, which was actually used by Qishuai Company on the accused infringing products. In addition, Wang Qiong also established Shenzhen Qishuai Company together with the legal representative of Shenzhen Siemens Company. It can be seen that, under circumstances where Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong had no connection whatsoever with Siemens Company or Siemens China Company, they engaged in multiple acts of free-riding on the reputation of the enterprises or registered trademarks of Siemens Company and Siemens China Company, either in the name of Qishuai Company or in other ways, demonstrating clear intentional infringement. The court of first instance found that these two individuals shared the intent to jointly infringe with Qishuai Company and constituted joint infringement with Qishuai Company. Therefore, it was not improper for this Court to hold that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should bear joint and several compensatory liability with Qishuai Company in this case, and this Court affirms that determination. However, the finding of the court of first instance that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong are husband and wife, that Qishuai Company should be regarded as a one-person company, and that Gong Yinqi and Wang Qiong should therefore bear joint and several liability with Qishuai Company lacked sufficient factual and legal basis. This Court hereby points this out.

In summary, the appeal claims and reasons of Qishuai Company, Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong cannot be established and should be dismissed. The judgment of the court of first instance had some unclear findings of fact and improper application of law, which should be corrected; however, the result of the judgment of the court of first instance was correct and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 57, Paragraph 2, and Article 58 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2013), Article 6, Paragraphs 2 and 4, and Article 17 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (as revised in 2017), Article 13, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 332 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 542,615 shall be borne jointly by Ningbo Qishuai Electric Appliance Co., Ltd., Gong Yinqi, and Wang Qiong.

This judgment is final.
